clue.text: Dismissed a member making potential explosive

parts.note: dismissed from a job means fired
MP, Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Someone sacked a Member of Parliament and so created a ticking political bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potential explosive' is the definition: firedamp is the methane gas that can explode in coal mines.
explanation.definitionFit: Firedamp is methane collecting in mines, a gas that can blow up when it meets a flame.

clue.text: Vessel in thin metal, something very old

indicators.note: the ship abbreviation sits inside the word for thin metal

parts.note: foil is metal rolled into a thin sheet
SS, steamship

explanation.surface: A boat wrapped in tinfoil, some ancient relic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' tempts as the definition, but SS (steamship) is the vessel; the definition is 'something very old'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fossil is the preserved remains of an ancient organism, or figuratively an outdated person.

clue.text: Angler about to pull in fish on river?

indicators.note: the first piece pulls in, takes inside it, the fish

parts.note: re means about, concerning
an eel is a fish
R, river

explanation.surface: A fisherman is about to land a catch on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts the river letter after the rest, as in a down clue one piece sits on another.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeler is one who reels in a line, as a fisherman does, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Dog in Russian cottage endlessly has to avoid daughter

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the last letter of the Russian word goes

parts.note: a dacha is a Russian country house
to shun is to keep away from
D, daughter

explanation.surface: A dog in a Russian cottage keeps away from the girl of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the final A from DACHA.
explanation.definitionFit: The dachshund is a long-bodied, short-legged German hound breed.

clue.text: Teasing 3 may do this -be quick about it!

definitions.meaning: 3 is the dog at 3-down; tease a dog and it may turn irritable and bite

explanation.surface: Bothering the dog will make it bad-tempered, so hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for hurry up, and literally means cause a dog to snap.

clue.text: Braved disturbance, delivering part of speech

indicators.note: a disturbance throws things into disorder, so the letters of the neighbouring word are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone bravely faced a riot while giving a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbance' tells you to rearrange BRAVED.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb is one of the grammatical word classes, modifying verbs and adjectives.

clue.text: A crazy upset about Rattigan's first play

indicators.note: about means around, so the reversed letters go round the initial
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the two pieces are read upwards

parts.note: mad means crazy

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the playwright's name

explanation.surface: Something crazy upsets a Rattigan premiere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns A MAD into DAMA; 'about' wraps that around R, Rattigan's first letter, after D. Terence Rattigan was an English playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Drama is another word for a play for the stage.

clue.text: Choose most exquisite — that's very exciting

parts.note: to elect is to choose

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its last letter

parts.note: rich means lavish, sumptuous, exquisite

explanation.surface: Picking the finest is thrilling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most' drops the final H of RICH.
explanation.definitionFit: Electric is used figuratively for thrilling, charged with excitement.

clue.text: Where flighty types may go for a walk in London?

definitions.text: Where flighty types may go for a walk in London?

parts.words: Where flighty types may go for a walk in London?
parts.note: flighty types are birds, which are kept in a cage

explanation.definitionFit: A cage for birds holds feathered creatures, and Birdcage Walk is a London street.

clue.text: Flavoured food children form into a mass

parts.note: seed means offspring, descendants, in the biblical sense
to cake is to clump together into a solid lump

explanation.surface: Kids squash their tasty snack into a lump.
explanation.walkthrough: SEED for children is the old biblical sense of descendants.
explanation.definitionFit: Seedcake is a cake flavoured with caraway seeds, so it is a seasoned foodstuff.

clue.text: Energy put into nurse's vocation

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside another, the letter going into the word for nurse

parts.note: a carer is someone who nurses; the possessive is just surface
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone puts all their energy into a nursing calling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put into' places the energy symbol inside the word for nurse, just before its final R.
explanation.definitionFit: A career is a person's chosen profession or calling in life.

clue.text: Break up earth, right? Finish harrowing

indicators.note: to break up something is to smash it to pieces, so the next word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: R, right
an ending is a finish

explanation.surface: Crumble the soil, then finish off with the harrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break up' rearranges EARTH into HEART. Harrowing looks like farming, but means distressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Heart-rending means deeply distressing, causing anguish.

clue.text: Articles for couples in romantic relationships

definitions.meaning: articles are separate things or objects in a list
two people who are dating are said to be an item

explanation.surface: Magazine features written for people in love.
explanation.definitionFit: Items are individual objects, and in slang a dating pair is an item, plural items.

clue.text: A client is crooked, but unlikely to do a stretch

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so the preceding letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A dishonest client probably won't end up serving time in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do a stretch' suggests a prison sentence, but here it means literally stretching.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inelastic cannot be pulled out longer, so it won't extend under tension.

clue.text: Excelling? Not in erotic entertainment

parts.note: someone not at home is out
stripping, undressing as a show

explanation.surface: Is it excellent to be absent from a strip show?
explanation.definitionFit: Outstripping is surpassing others, doing better than them.

clue.text: Ample for poet — unless cut short, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals another possible arrangement of the letters
cut short means losing the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Something is enough for a poet, unless it is trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' takes the last S off UNLESS; 'possibly' rearranges POET plus UNLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Plenteous is a literary word for plentiful, abundant.

clue.text: Unspecified amount in current test for equality of measure

indicators.note: the vague quantity sits inside the other two pieces

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
a try is an attempt or test
some is an indefinite quantity

explanation.surface: A vague quantity in an electrical test checks that things are equal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unspecified amount in current' looks like one unit, but the vague amount sits inside current and test together.
explanation.definitionFit: Isometry is equality of dimensions, a transformation preserving distances.

clue.text: One of those collaborators in France who hang

parts.note: qui is French for who
to sling is to hang loosely or suspend

explanation.surface: Some French collaborators were hanged after the war.
explanation.walkthrough: A quisling, after Norwegian Vidkun Quisling, is a traitor who collaborates with an occupying enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: A quisling is a traitor who works with an invading power, like the wartime collaborators.

clue.text: Sturdy obstruction easily broken by Jumbo

parts.note: sound means solid and in good condition
a barrier blocks the way

explanation.surface: A strong fence that an elephant tramples with ease.
explanation.walkthrough: Jumbo suggests an elephant, but it is a jumbo jet, which flies faster than sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Supersonic aircraft pass the speed of sound, so the wall of air resistance is broken by a big jet.

clue.text: Run through small change accepted by one fellow

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: accepted by means taken inside the other two pieces

parts.note: a male is a fellow, a man
P, penny, a small coin

explanation.surface: One man takes a few pennies after running through his money.
explanation.walkthrough: P goes between I and MALE.
explanation.definitionFit: To impale is to pierce through with a sharp stake or spike.

clue.text: Changing sides, collar and put in enclosure

indicators.note: the sides are left and right, so the L and R letters swap places

explanation.surface: Turn the collar inside out and keep it penned in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changing sides' swaps each L (left) for R (right) and the R for L in COLLAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To corral is to drive livestock into a pen.

clue.text: Distorted representation of ship's name

indicators.note: a fresh representation re-presents the letters, giving them in another order

explanation.surface: A ship's name has been shown in a warped form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'representation of' signals an anagram of SHIPS plus NAME; here the 's of ship's counts as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Misshapen means deformed, out of its proper shape.

clue.text: Mac's impatient cry produces shouts of laughter

definitions.meaning: a Scottish exclamation of irritation; Mac stands for a Scot

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's grumble only makes people laugh.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scots interjection is an exclamation of impatience, and the plural noun means loud guffaws.

clue.text: The going rate for musicians

parts.note: reads like a standard fee for a band, but means the speed at which a piece of music goes

explanation.definitionFit: Tempo is the pace at which music is played, the speed a performer keeps.

clue.text: Interval shortened for appearance of sea-god

indicators.note: shortened tells us to cut the final letter from the musical word

parts.note: a tritone is a musical interval of three whole tones

explanation.surface: After a brief pause, a god of the sea makes an entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortened' drops the last E from TRITONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Triton is the Greek merman deity, son of Poseidon, who blows a conch shell.

clue.text: Greek character swallowed by relatively small monster

indicators.note: one piece is swallowed, taken inside, the word for comparatively small

parts.note: minor means lesser, comparatively small
tau is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek is eaten by a monster that is fairly small.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relatively small' is a comparative, which is why it gives MINOR rather than a plain word for little.
explanation.definitionFit: The Minotaur was the bull-headed beast of Cretan legend kept in the labyrinth.

clue.text: Philosophical Hindu's practice is to interrupt my go, oddly

indicators.note: the little word breaks into the jumbled letters, sitting between them
behaving oddly means strangely, so the two short words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Hindu thinker's ritual involves cutting in on my turn in a strange manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' shuffles the two short words; 'to interrupt' then breaks into that jumble just before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Yogism is the doctrine and discipline followed by a yogi in Hindu philosophy.

clue.text: Delicate porcelain smashed before soldiers go in

definitions.meaning: a very thin, fragile type of china
soldiers are strips of toast dipped into a boiled egg once its top is cracked open

explanation.surface: Fine china is broken before troops advance.
explanation.walkthrough: Soldiers are British breakfast toast fingers dunked into a soft-boiled egg, not troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggshell china is extremely thin porcelain, and an egg's outer casing is cracked before toast fingers dip in.
